title: people-ops self notes + manager prep - Q1 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal notes for manager 1:1 + self-review prep. Drafted as bullet points so I can bring up specific asks and examples.

Accomplishments (last 6-9 months):
- Reduced new-hire time-to-first-contribution from ~18 days -> 10 days (measured cohort Nov 2025–Jan 2026) by standardizing onboarding checklist and automating account provisioning with infra team.
- Launched async onboarding playbook and ‘first-week checklist’ doc; 92% of new hires reported clarity on expectations in new-hire survey (n=50).
- Ran 3 calibration sessions with Eng/Product/Design leads to formalize leveling guidance for ICs; created candidate rubric that was adopted for hiring panel use.
- Piloted manager enablement workshops (2 sessions, 24 managers) to improve 1:1 quality; baseline pulse survey showed +0.4 increase in manager confidence metric.
- Implemented a simple learning stipend workflow (Stripe + People Ops approval) and tracked initial uptake: 18 employees in first month.
- Supported two org restructures with offboarding/onboarding coordination and role mapping; preserved headcount targets and minimized disruption.

What I’m proud of (examples to call out):
- Saved ~20 engineering hours per hire by automating cloud account provisioning with infra (worked closely with Keita and Arjun).
- A very positive cross-functional retrospective after the product org restructure — leads said communication from People Ops was the best part.

Areas for improvement / missed things:
- Metrics instrumentation: still manually compiling hiring/handover metrics for exec reports. Need to partner with analytics to automate reporting.
- DEI initiative: rollout slower than planned; must push to prioritize candidate-sourcing partnerships and structured interview training.
- Need a clearer 6-month roadmap for manager enablement (we have workshops but no cadence or enablement owner).

Goals (next 6 months):
- Operational: Automate the monthly hiring and onboarding dashboard (time-to-hire, time-to-first-contrib, offer acceptance) so execs can view live metrics. Target: MVP by end of Q2 2026.
- People programs: Formalize manager enablement program — create a quarterly cadence, templated 1:1 agendas, and manager FAQ. Owner: me + solutions engineering partner.
- Strategic: Build an internal leveling guide for ICs (draft v1) with clear behavioral examples for L2–L6. Pilot in Eng and Product.
- Cost/process: Reduce manual steps in offer acceptance flow by 30% (target fewer spreadsheets and email threads).

Requests for manager (things I want to discuss / ask for):
- Promotion roadmap: I want to understand expectations/timeline for Senior People Ops (IC3) promotion — what concrete milestones should I hit over the next 3–6 months?
- Headcount ask: Request to open a 0.5 FTE for People Ops Program Coordinator to own recurring onboarding tasks (freeing me to focus on the manager enablement program). Have a draft JD and cost estimate.
- Analytics partnership: Can you help unblock a seat at the table with Product Analytics so we can get the onboarding dashboard prioritized? I can scope the metrics but need their bandwidth.
- Visibility: Would love a recurring 15-min sync with you before the exec HR report so we can align messaging and any escalations.

Feedback for manager / notes I want to say in 1:1:
- Appreciate that you’ve been supportive of cross-team work — a quick ask: help signal to Eng leads that People Ops should be included early in project planning (especially infra changes that affect onboarding).
- Would like more direct feedback on asynchronous leadership (doc reviews). Maybe a monthly doc-review slot?

Risks / blockers I want to highlight:
- Analytics bandwidth (no reliable SLA) — delaying the onboarding dashboard and exec reporting.
- Competing priorities on infra: provisioning automation needs a follow-up sprint to clear remaining edge cases.
- Hiring freeze possibility if execs reprioritize; outline contingency plan (prioritize critical hires, delay non-critical training events).

Concrete next steps (my proposed 30/60/90):
- 30 days: Finalize program coordinator JD, align with finance on cost, ask you to approve headcount conversation. Start scoping onboarding dashboard with analytics (list top 8 metrics).
- 60 days: Pilot manager enablement cadence with 1 team (Eng). Deliver v0.1 of IC leveling guide.
- 90 days: Dashboard MVP running (weekly update), present promotion milestones for my role, and hire or convert PT contractor to cover coordinator work.

Notes to self / script for 1:1:
- Quick wins to mention: onboarding time reduction, provisioning automation savings (20h/hire), workshop feedback scores.
- Big asks: 0.5 FTE coordinator, analytics champion, clear promo rubric for IC3.
- Keep tone: pragmatic, evidence-based, offer tradeoffs (I can own the manager program if admin work is covered).

Open questions I want help resolving:
- What’s the preferred promotion timeline for IC people ops at Redwood (benchmarks from other functions)?
- Is there budget runway for a fractional coordinator in Q2? If not, propose contractor.

Quick links / references:
- ONBOARDING PLAYBOOK (link to confluence page) — draft v2 (waiting review)
- JIRA-PEOPLE-128 — onboarding dashboard epic
- Calibration rubric draft (shared drive link)

End of notes.

(Will trim and convert to a tidy manager prep doc after our 1:1 — these are raw talking points.)
